question: The Ghadar Party, established in 1913 in San Francisco, aimed to overthrow the British rule in India through revolutionary means. Who was the key founder and ideological leader of the Ghadar Party?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Har Dayal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lala Har Dayal** was the key founder and ideological leader of the **Ghadar Party**, established in 1913 in San Francisco.
 
• The Ghadar Party was founded with the aim of overthrowing British rule in India through **revolutionary means**.
 
• Lala Har Dayal was a scholar, revolutionary, and ardent advocate of freedom, who inspired Indian immigrants in the United States and Canada to join the struggle for India's independence.
 
• The name "Ghadar" was derived from the Urdu word for "mutiny" or "rebellion," symbolizing the party's aim to incite an armed uprising against British colonial rule.
 
• Under Lala Har Dayal's leadership, the Ghadar Party launched the **"Ghadar Newspaper"**, a weekly publication that galvanized Indians worldwide to support the revolutionary movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghadar Party:**

 
 
• The Ghadar Party was primarily composed of Indian immigrants, notably Sikhs and Punjabis, living in the United States and Canada.
 
• It aimed to inspire Indians across the globe to unite and fight against British imperialism.
 
• The party's headquarters, called the "Yugantar Ashram," was based in San Francisco.
 
 
 
• **Lala Har Dayal's Ideology:**
 
 
• Lala Har Dayal was influenced by a mix of socialist, anarchist, and nationalist ideas.
 
• He believed in the power of education and self-reliance as tools to achieve political freedom.
 
 
 
• **Other Key Figures:**
 
 
• While Lala Har Dayal was the ideological leader, other prominent members included **Sohan Singh Bhakna** and Kartar Singh Sarabha.
 
• Kartar Singh Sarabha, though young, became a symbol of sacrifice and dedication within the Ghadar movement.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Ghadar Movement:**
 
 
• The movement laid the foundation for revolutionary activities in India and abroad.
 
• Though it failed to achieve its immediate goal, the Ghadar Party's efforts significantly influenced subsequent nationalist movements.
